Kessel.et: From Middle High German keȥȥel, from Old High German keȥȥil, from Proto-West Germanic *katil (“kettle”).

Kescher.et: Borrowed from Middle Low German kesser. A relation with English catch, catcher is possible, though direct borrowing (as assumed by Kluge, edition 24) seems doubtful.

Kesselschlacht.et: Compound of Kessel (“pocket (of units); kettle, cauldron”) + Schlacht (“battle”).

Kessenich.et: Both places are first attested with -st- (Castnec, Castenicha, 9th c.). Therefore thought to be from Latin *Castenacum or *Castaniacum. Alternatively perhaps from *Cassiniacum like the Dutch above.
